thread:
maya: Quick sync — proposing a 'slimline' observability launch for Console. Goal: deliver minimal dashboards + cheap tracing hooks + cost breakdown + basic error analytics by end of Q2. Focus is on high-impact signals for product teams, not full fidelity right away.

sam: +1 on tight scope. what's our hard cutoff for "minimal"?

maya: Minimal = 3 dashboards (latency p50/p95 by route, cost by model+route, errors by service+code), single tracing hook that captures 1 span/sample per request with trace_id propagation, and an error sink that tags customer-request-id. Launch criteria: dashboards live, trace hook deployed in canary, cost numbers matching billing within 10%, and a playbook doc for oncall.

leah: Sampling 1 span/request sounds fine, but need clar on overhead. If we sample every request across high-throughput routes we'll spike CPU. Recommend adaptive sampling: full sample for errors, 1% for normal traffic, and a per-route override.

sam: Technical constraints: our runtime currently batches token streaming; adding synchronous trace emission can add tail latency. Plan: async buffered trace flush with max_delay=200ms, and use a lightweight proto for spans. Example config snippet: `trace.flush_delay_ms=200`, `trace.sample_pct=1`.

ivan: For cost breakdown, teams want model-level attribution + route tags. We need a deterministic token counter per request and route tag propagation into billing pipeline. Proposed metric names: `redwood.cost.tokens_per_request`, `redwood.cost.model_id`, `redwood.route.name`. How do we ensure these line up with upstream billing?

todd: Ivan — tie the acceptance test to billing sandbox: run a controlled workload, assert cost report within 10% for model-level buckets. Also require a small customer-facing doc describing what cost lines mean.

maya: Customer asks we captured: (1) show model delta in cost dashboard, (2) quick drill from error spike -> traces, (3) alert on cost growth >20% w/ root cause pointer. We should prioritize (1) + (3) for launch, (2) can be soft-linked to follow-up.

leah: For alerting: suggest two SLO gates — error-rate by route (5xx% threshold) and token-cost drift by week. Alert routes should include runbook links and suggested mitigations (roll back to smaller model, enable caching).

sam: FYI — runtime work to emit route tags + token counters is ~3 engineer-weeks (core runtime + client SDK changes) unless we scope to only HTTP routes (no websocket streaming) for launch. Recommend dropping websocket coverage for v1.

maya: I'm fine dropping websocket for v1 if it reduces risk. We should call out in the launch notes: "websocket sampling & tracing coming in v1.1".

ivan: Data infra: cost aggregation pipeline needs a TTL-friendly retention (30d fine for v1) and pre-aggregation by (customer, model, route). We'll provide a QA dataset for acceptance.

ops-bot: Deploy window available: 2026-05-18 02:00-04:00 UTC for canary -> 2026-05-19 03:00-06:00 UTC for rollout.

todd: Next steps: 1) eng to post a short RFC with exact metric names + sampling algorithm by EOD Fri, 2) product to draft customer-facing cost doc, 3) SRE run a perf test on trace flush strategy.

maya: I'll own the RFC & customer doc drafts. Sam/leah/ivan — can you confirm ETA for your pieces?

sam: Eng RFC by Fri, sampling impl spike complete in 5bd, canary plan attached to RFC.

leah: Perf test plan by Tue next week, will validate CPU + tail latency with trace.enabled=true.

ivan: Data QA dataset + aggregation job by Wed.

todd: I'll schedule a 30min triage on Monday to lock acceptance tests.

maya: Thanks — if we hit those dates we should be on track for the May deploy window. Reaction if you agree: :rocket: :eyes: 

sam: :rocket:

leah: :eyes:

ivan: :+1:

ops-bot: Noted: canary window reserved.
